content.text:
I fixed it with a one-line change to the inline `br` rule in `src/rules.ts:286`. I haven't run anything: there's no `node_modules`, so neither the tests nor your example have been tried against the change. **Cause:** the hard-break rule matched only the trailing spaces (or backslash) and the newline: ```ts const br = /^( {2,}|\\)\n(?!\s*$)/; ``` Any spaces or tabs at the start of the next line were left in the remaining text. The text rule then output them, which gave `

foo
bar

`. **Fix:** the break token now also takes in the spaces and tabs that follow the newline: ```ts const br = /^( {2,}|\\)\n[ \t]*(?!\s*$)/; ``` - **What's covered:** the change handles both forms in the report, two-or-more trailing spaces and a trailing backslash, and leading tabs as well as spaces. - **No break at the end of a paragraph:** the lookahead `(?!\s*$)` still stops a break from matching when only whitespace follows, so that case behaves as before. - **`breaks: true` mode:** the GFM version of the rule is built from this one (`edit(br).replace('{2,}', '*')`), so it gets the same fix. In that mode, a plain newline followed by an indented line now drops the indentation too, which is the behaviour the report asks for.
